title: A Road That Isn’t a Road

lines.en: Immediately after <Olympus>'s <Gigantomachia> collapsed, the restrictions binding the giants vanished. Freed from their ancient Story, they would now become participants in new scenarios.
[I have no wish to repeat our predecessors' battle. Do you agree?]
[I agree.]
And so, with the end of Scenario 60 just ahead, Briareus, leader of the giants, and Dionysus, temporary representative of the 12 Seats, reached a dramatic agreement.
[<Star Stream> acknowledges the ‘collapse of the myth’.]
[A new Story blooms in Scenario 60.]
In truth, they might have been able to keep fighting if they wanted to.

But <Gigantomachia> had drastically weakened <Olympus>'s fighting strength. Many heroes and giants had died, the whereabouts of ‘Poseidon’ were unknown, and the silent ‘King of the Underworld’ had announced his successor.
If the remaining 12 Seats and the giants continued their confrontation now, they would only endanger the nebula's existence.
The fall of the great nebula <Olympus>.
At the center of that incredible story was one small nebula.
[Many constellations chant the name ‘Kim Dokja's Company’!]
That story, which had begun with one small constellation's struggle, was at last bringing a ‘Giant Story’ to its close.
Yet the members of that nebula had no time to savor the lingering emotion of the ending of the ‘Giant Story’. They were calling someone's name.
“Dokja-ssi! Dokja-ssi!”
“Hyung! Stop playing around! Where are you hiding?”
Jung Heewon, Lee Hyunsung, Lee Jihye, Shin Yoosung, Lee Gilyoung······.
They were searching for Kim Dokja on a small island the giants had made.
Some with anxious voices, others with disbelieving faces.
Amid the confusion, the only one who remained calm was a man gazing up at the sky without expression.
Han Sooyoung glared intently at him, then asked:
“Yoo Joonghyuk. You know something, don't you?”
“Answer me. The kids are worried.”
Yoo Joonghyuk slowly turned toward Han Sooyoung.
Noticing something, the others gathered behind her.
“What is it, Master? Do you know something?”
“Nothing's happened to Dokja-ssi again, has it?”
After a short silence, Yoo Joonghyuk answered.
“Kim Dokja will have returned to Earth.”
“What? Without us?”
Realization belatedly dawned on Lee Jihye, and her mouth fell slightly open.
“Ah······Could it be?”

Come to think of it, <Gigantomachia> hadn't been their real objective. Participating in it had been only a step along the way. While everyone else was intoxicated with victory, Kim Dokja alone had been thinking about the real purpose of all this.
Jung Heewon let out a sigh of relief and said with a wry smile:
“······Even so, I'll have a few things to say about him running straight home by himself.”
“Let's hurry back, too!”
Just then, a system message appeared.
[Leaving the area is restricted for 1 hour to stabilize the scenario.]
Lee Seolhwa asked, her eyes wide with surprise.
“······How on earth did Dokja-ssi get out?”
“He probably used some special method.”
“A special method?”
“I don't know the details, either.”
With that answer, Yoo Joonghyuk looked up at the sky again.
Snow was still falling. Snow fluttering through brilliant summer weather. On Earth, it would have been like snow falling in August.
Watching it, Han Sooyoung asked Yoo Joonghyuk:
“······Kim Dokja went back first because of Yoo Sangah, didn't he?”
There was always a reason to ask the obvious.
Yoo Joonghyuk answered only after the miraculous flurry had melted away in the sunlight.
“We'll find out when we get there.”
Inside the car racing along a dimensional road (次元路), I briefly lost myself in thought.
When I first began planning to overturn <Gigantomachia>, I contacted several constellations. Probably every constellation who was even slightly acquainted with me received a message.
Most had special ties to <Olympus> or circumstances that made joining Scenario 60 difficult. I understood. What constellation would want to make an enemy of a great nebula like <Olympus>?
But one of them made an unusual offer.
―I cannot help you with <Gigantomachia>. But I can open an escape route if you fail. For you alone, however.
And the one who had made that offer now sat at ease in the driver's seat, holding the wheel.
[······I never imagined you'd use my offer like this.]
A being who could pass through a ‘scenario’ portal with his own probability, and the owner of a [Special Ferrarghini] that could travel dimensional roads at will.
‘Mass Production Maker’ smiled as he spoke.
[You used to be the sort who rarely asked anyone for help.]
“My thinking changed a little after I visited another worldline.”
I smiled and added:
“Besides, I accidentally left my [X-grade Ferrarghini] behind. I haven't even finished paying the installments. I still tear up whenever I think about it.”
[Hahaha. You mean the car you bought from me?]
“So I've decided to stop driving my own car and get rides in other people's cars from now on.”
[Oh dear. As the seller, I find that a regrettable decision. A new model just came out, and I was going to give you one for free.]
“······For free?”
[I'm lying.]
······I knew it. That sly old constellation would never willingly take a loss.

With a thick cigar between his lips, ‘Mass Production Maker’ seemed to consider something for a moment. The drifting smoke was sucked into a vent in front of the glove compartment before it could reach me in the passenger seat.
[I'd like to make a ‘contract’ with your nebula.]
“A contract?”
[Do you realize what you've done this time?]
I knew.
How could I not?
[The Giant Story ‘Torch That Swallowed the Myth’ flows through your Story veins (說脈)!]
Even now, the ‘result’ of what I'd done was flowing through every vein in my body.
「Torch That Swallowed the Myth」.

It wasn't 「One Who Erases God's Fingerprints」 or 「One Who Closes the Gate of Myth」, the Stories I'd originally wanted. But its essence was similar. A Story earned by fighting a great nebula and overturning a myth. It would serve as a counter to the countless nebulas I would fight in the future.
[What happened has made many constellations aware of <Kim Dokja's Company>.]
“I imagine so.”
[Some even insist that your nebula should be counted among the <Twelve Great Nebulas>.]
······The Twelve Great Nebulas. It didn't feel real that I'd already reached a position where I could hear that said about us.

The twelve nebulas that dominated <Star Stream>: three strong (强), four middle (中), and five weak (弱). <Olympus>, which had fluctuated between the top three and the middle four, had just suffered a heavy blow. Someone was bound to try to fill the gap.
“A lot of stars are getting ahead of themselves.”
[That's how the gossipmongers always are.]
“And you, ‘Mass Production Maker’, would like to take the opportunity to sign a contract with our nebula.”
[Precisely.]
There wasn't a trace of hesitation in his answer.
[I'm thinking of having your nebula advertise my new product. What do you say?]
“I'd be happy to. I'll ask the others in the nebula, too.”
[Excellent. As for the incarnations I'd personally like to appear······.]

Listening to ‘Mass Production Maker’, I watched the scenery pass beyond the [Ferrarghini]'s window. Countless seasons of stories flowed through that passing landscape. From spring to summer, then autumn.
Yes. Before I knew it······.
“······It's fast.”
The words slipped out as I gripped the bottle of Star Relic Liquid against my chest.
I'd made it this far faster than in any round of the original novel. But that speed was only relative. I didn't know whether it was ‘fast enough’.
‘Mass Production Maker’ laughed heartily as he spoke.
[This new model is rather fast. You'll see if you drive it yourself, but the handling is absolutely······.]
“It's taking an awfully long time for the speed we're doing. You're not taking a detour just to discuss the contract, are you?”
[Ahem. What are you talking about? This is the fastest route. Look, we're already at the last junction.]
As ‘Mass Production Maker’ said, three portals were shining white across the pitch-black dimensional road. Without being asked, ‘Mass Production Maker’ added an explanation.
[One leads to Earth. Another leads to the ‘context of my constellation’.]
“What about the last one?”
[A ‘road that looks like a road’.]
Mass Production Maker said with a meaningful smile.
A portal much darker than the others, giving off a damp, gloomy air.
[Do you know what's at the end of it?]
Of course, I didn't.
Not even ‘Ways of Survival’ described every portal along the dimensional roads. In other words, that ‘portal’ would be a road that didn't exist in ‘Ways of Survival’.
“What's there?”
[Nothing. It's simply a dead end.]
An answer delivered as though it were perfectly obvious.
Before I could reply, ‘Mass Production Maker’ continued.
[Some roads end like that. You walk them because they look different, or because you think no one has taken them before. But often, they weren't even roads to begin with.]
The [Ferrarghini] accelerated past the gloomy portal. The glowing navigation display showed the route to Earth.
On the screen, the portal we'd just passed was marked ‘No Road’.
[Such roads usually break off in some uncertain place. And those who chose to walk them must go on living, believing that was the end.]
“······What are you trying to tell me?”
[Please choose your road carefully.]
‘Mass Production Maker’, who had already put out his cigar, spoke with his usual gentlemanly smile.
[Sometimes, what looked like a road may never have been a road at all.]
The next moment, the dimensional scenery changed. I caught a glimpse of a blue planet, and suddenly I had landed on the ground.
‘Mass Production Maker’ spoke.
[We're here. Fortunately, it seems we arrived at the right place this time.]
The place I headed for as soon as I reached Seoul was, needless to say, the [Factory]. More specifically, the ward where the patients were staying.
The moment I stepped inside, a voice almost like a [True Voice] rang out.
[You've come.]
It sounded like a [True Voice], but it wasn't one. A voice bearing a transcendent's dignity.
Baekchung's magic power, crackling blue in the air.
······It seemed all masters wanted their disciples to see them in the same light, after all.
“Your unworthy disciple greets you.”
[We have no time. I'll accept your greeting later. Go.]
Kyrgios was wrapped in bandages, perhaps from the ‘Returnee War’.
“What about the Blood Demon and the Heavenly Demon······?”
[I killed them. Stop talking and go.]

I inwardly marveled at that calm declaration. He had faced the Blood Demon and the Heavenly Demon alone, opponents even the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint of a previous life couldn't defeat, and survived. I could barely grasp how much stronger my master had grown in this round.
Aileen spotted me from a distance and came running. The only Story Expert guarding the [Factory]. Without her, two or three of our companions would already have died.
I pulled the Star Relic Liquid from my coat and waved it as I shouted:
“I brought Star Relic Liquid!”
“There's something I didn't get a chance to tell you······.”
“I know the situation.”
Two hospital rooms glowed red in the distance.
One was Yoo Sangah's. The other······.
“How is my mother?”
“Her symptoms are almost the same as Yoo Sangah-ssi's.”
“How severe?”
“If anything, they're worse. Certainly no less······.”
I knew my mother had been pushing herself too hard.

Stigmas that foresaw the ‘great future’ put a heavy burden on their users. That burden would have been far worse for Yoo Sangah, whose contract with an entire nebula was ambiguous, and my mother, whose sponsor had lost almost all her power.
Taking the liquid from me, Aileen spoke in a grim voice.
“I don't think this will be enough.”
“That's why I brought two bottles. Different kinds, too.”
I hadn't brought just one kind. Besides the [Soma] Surya had promised, I had the [Nectar] I'd taken from Dionysus.
For a moment, Aileen's face brightened as she took the two bottles.
“······Medical team!”

The physicians who ran over at her signal headed for the two rooms all at once. Someone brushed against me on the way past, sending a fierce ache through the side Poseidon had struck. My vision blurred for a moment, then cleared.
······Maybe I needed treatment, too.
Then again, it would have been stranger to be fine after taking a Myth-grade constellation's attack.

I forced myself to steady my breathing to hide the pain. Perhaps because my consciousness was unstable, the doors the physicians entered looked just like the portals ‘Mass Production Maker’ had shown me.
[Are you all right?]
Kyrgios flew over to ask me. I answered that I was fine. More precisely, I seemed to have answered, and also to have lost consciousness for a moment.
When I came to, I was lying on a chair in the ward.
Aileen stood before me.
Enduring the pain, I got up.
“······How are they?”
I forced my clouding consciousness into focus as I asked.
But there was something wrong with Aileen's expression.
“······It's not enough.”
“Not enough? What isn't?”
“Their conditions worsened much faster than we expected. I think we'd need both bottles of Star Relic Liquid just to treat one of them.”
I couldn't understand her. In that moment, Aileen's words sounded like a distant alien language. Like an Outer God's gibberish.
“What······does that mean?”
“Demon King of Salvation-nim.”
It had been a long time since Aileen addressed me by my modifier. She only called me that when she needed an order.
The two rooms stood wide open, like portals waiting for me.
“We can save only one person.”
All kinds of thoughts flashed through my head.
[‘Fourth Wall’ shakes violently.]
There were two doors. It was as though someone were whispering to me.
Go in, if you want.
But if you choose one, you must abandon the other.
······There was no way I could.
“Demon King of Salvation-nim.”
“If you delay any longer, we won't be able to save either of them.”
Aileen's voice sounded unreal.
“Please give me a moment.”
As my vision swam, I could see the ward's corridor running between the two rooms.
The words of ‘Mass Production Maker’ crossed my mind.
―Nothing. It's simply a dead end.
The corridor's end was too dark to see, but everyone knew there was nothing there.
A corridor designed to have nothing at its end.
「Kim Dokja thought: That can't be right.」
Stay calm. There is a way.
I'd come all this way, and now I had to choose one of them?
Who was I supposed to save, and who was I supposed to kill?
I couldn't do that.
[‘Fourth Wall’ looks at you.]
「B u t you've cho sen be fore.」
The ‘first scenario’ flashed through my head. The swaying subway. People lying dead. People I might have been able to save—all of them.
「S o you can cho ose a gain this time.」
······This isn't like then.
「W hat's dif fer ent?」
Instead of answering [Fourth Wall], I asked Aileen:
“How much time do we have?”
“About twenty minutes······Lee Sookyung-ssi is in a slightly more critical condition. If more time passes, even that will no longer be······.”
Twenty minutes.
Not long, but enough to try a few things.
It was too early to give up.
“If we had more Star Relic Liquid, could we save them both?”
“······There might be a chance.”
I immediately took out [Old to New Toad].
With a croak, the toad spoke.
―G ive me the old, I'll give you the new.
I pointed to the half-full bottle of [Nectar] and asked:
“Could you exchange this for a ‘new’ one, too?”
But [Old to New Toad] shook its head.
―T hat is nei ther old nor new.
“I drank half of this. That makes it old. I'll give you another item, so if you could refill this bottle to make it new again······.”
―S oph is try······That isn't some thing I can grant.
As expected, it seemed tricks like this wouldn't work on an item like Star Relic Liquid. I'd thought it might work.
―I'm ti red. Don't ca ll me.
Perhaps swallowing the ‘Giant Soldier’ and making it new earlier had exhausted it. With those words, [Old to New Toad] fell fast asleep.
I put it away and decided to try a second method.
If I couldn't duplicate it, I'd have to get more.
[Demon King ‘Demon King of Salvation’······.]
Tzzzzzt!
[Indirect message use has been canceled.]
[Indirect messages are currently disabled due to maintenance and repairs on a particular scenario.]
[The scenario under maintenance is ‘Scenario 60’.]
An unforeseen coincidence. I hadn't imagined the fierce fighting in Scenario 60 would have repercussions all the way here······.
But I needed help from other constellations to get more Star Relic Liquid.
“Jang Hayoung!”
At my shout, Aileen looked in a certain direction.
As luck would have it, Jang Hayoung was hospitalized in Yoo Sangah's room. A chill crept over the back of my neck as I stood on the threshold beneath the emergency light.
“You can't just come in!”
Someone shouted at me.
Story fragments drifted through the air from where Yoo Sangah lay.
I forced myself to look away and pushed past the physicians to find Jang Hayoung.
Jang Hayoung lay asleep in the room's right-hand corner.
“Jang Hayoung! Wake up! Hurry!”
“Wait! That patient is in critical condition, too!”
The physicians rushed over to pull me back.
Looking closer, I saw that Jang Hayoung was wrapped in bandages and receiving a large number of Story Packs. The ‘Returnee War’ had left Hayoung badly injured, too.
But I desperately needed Jang Hayoung's skill.
[‘Unidentifiable Wall’ looks at you.]
[‘Fourth Wall’ faces ‘Unidentifiable Wall’.]
Sparks flickered before me, and I felt the wall's impersonal gaze.
An icy indifference without the slightest desire to cooperate.
······So that's how you want to play it?
I opened [Bookmark].
In the end, ‘Unidentifiable Wall’ was a ‘skill,’ too.
My understanding of ‘Jang Hayoung’ was still low, so I'd need a little luck······.
I began searching the [Bookmark] list for the name ‘Jang Hayoung’.
Perhaps sensing something unpleasant in my actions, ‘Unidentifiable Wall’ spoke in warning.
[‘Unidentifiable Wall’ says: ‘You are not my master. Don't do anything useless.’]
“I need your help.”
I spoke honestly. Every minute, every second, counted.
“If you don't help me, I'll have to wake your master.”
For a while, the wall didn't answer. Silence, as though it were thinking something over.
After a moment, a message came from the other side.
[‘Unidentifiable Wall’ says: ‘······I'll help.’]
At those words, a small partitioned space formed around me. It reminded me of my office long ago, when I was an intern at Mino Soft.
A large panel that had formed in front of me, with a familiar-looking input device beneath it.

Jang Hayoung had probably listened to countless constellations' stories inside this narrow wall. Jang Hayoung, who must have listened, listened, and listened again to stories like scribbles that could be written only on this small wall······.
[‘Unidentifiable Wall’ says: ‘You should have been nicer all along.’]
······I had nothing to say to that.
I looked down briefly at the sleeping Jang Hayoung, then turned away.
First, I had to put out the immediate fire.
[‘Unidentifiable Wall’ has temporarily granted you ‘permission to use’ it.]
[Enter the recipient of your message.]
The first constellation who came to mind was Dionysus.
[You cannot send a message to this constellation.]
[All communications with the nebula <Olympus> are currently unavailable.]
I'd hit a wall from the start.
I quickly changed the message's recipient.
A reply came immediately.
―You need more Soma? I'm sorry, but······what I gave you was all the Soma I had.
It was from Surya.
As expected, things weren't going well on that end, either.
―Would it be difficult to request more from your nebula?
―I lost my production rights for Soma when I left <Vedas>.
―Is Dionysus with you?
Perhaps understanding my intention, Surya answered a moment later.
―<Olympus> has also been suffering a Story famine recently, so the supply of ‘Nectar’ has stopped. He says there isn't enough left to spare any for you.
―I understand. Thank you.
―I'm sorry I couldn't help.
―Please don't be.
Surya had already helped me so much during <Gigantomachia>. I couldn't ask anything more of him.
I recalled the various Star Relic Liquids that appeared in ‘Ways of Survival’. But of the things that could replace [Nectar] and [Soma], none were within immediate reach.
Biting my lip, I thought desperately.
If treatment was impossible, I could find another way.
[Sending a message to constellation ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring’.]
Persephone and Hades didn't belong to <Olympus>, so I could contact them through ‘Unidentifiable Wall’. I hadn't wanted to use this method, but I couldn't afford to be picky.
Yet Persephone's answer wasn't very encouraging, either.
―My son, as you know, a being shattered by 「stream of consciousness」······.
Every soul in this world went to the ‘Underworld’.
But only if the soul was intact.
―······So that's how it is.
In truth, I'd expected it to some extent.
「stream of consciousness」 was a condition in which the stories making up a soul broke apart.
A soul suffering from it didn't go to the <Underworld>.
More precisely, it didn't go anywhere.
It simply ended there. Disappearing forever on that spot, like someone collapsing at the end of the wrong road.
Persephone spoke.
―My son.
―I haven't properly taken up the role of ‘heir’ yet. Please don't call me that now.
I replied quickly, cut the connection, and opened the ‘Ways of Survival’ file on my smartphone.
There was still a way. There had to be.
[‘Unidentifiable Wall’ says: ‘You have harmed too much probability.’]
······Shut up.
[‘Unidentifiable Wall’ says: ‘The probability you harm will always come back to you. That is the law of this world.’]
“I said shut up.”
I rapidly read through ‘Ways of Survival’.
Searching it, I found that the Yoo Joonghyuk of ‘Ways of Survival’ had faced similar predicaments a few times.
The 161st and 275th rounds, for example.
In those rounds, Yoo Joonghyuk faced situations where he could save only one of two companions.
Told he could save only Lee Seolhwa or Lee Jihye, he answered:
「“I'll save them both.”」
It was the same in the 275th round.
Lee Hyunsung and Shin Yoosung. When he could rescue only one of them, Yoo Joonghyuk declared:
「“I will save them both.”」
An answer truly worthy of Yoo Joonghyuk.
And so, the Yoo Joonghyuks of the 161st and 275th rounds failed.
He saved neither Lee Seolhwa nor Lee Jihye, neither Lee Hyunsung nor Shin Yoosung.
Nor, in the end, himself.
Yet every time, Yoo Joonghyuk made the same choice, and then the same choice again.
My right hand trembled uneasily as I held the screen, so I gripped that hand tightly.
「B ut Kim Dok ja isn't Yoo Joong hyuk.」
Yoo Joonghyuk could make that choice because he was a regressor.
A regressor, unlike me. Someone who could repeat his life many times.
But this life was all I had.
And so it allowed me no mistakes.
If I made a mistake, someone would die.
That was why I hadn't made mistakes.
I'd twisted the flow and made it this far despite having to bear the distorted probability.
I thought I'd done well to get this far.
Briareus had said:
―True 'Fate' cannot be avoided. If you evade it, probability will inevitably be distorted. And someone must always resolve that distorted probability in your place.
I knew. I'd heard that, too.
The only thing I couldn't accept was:
Why.
Why······did they have to be the ones to resolve it?
「Dokja-ssi.」
One drop. Two drops.
A voice touching me like water droplets boring through solid granite.
I turned around.
「Dokja-ssi, I'm all right.」
Broken Story fragments streamed from between the curtains around Yoo Sangah's bed, rippling toward me and speaking.
「Save Sookyung-ssi.」
My mouth hung half-open, but no sound came out.
Yet Yoo Sangah answered as though she'd heard me.
「There's a way for me to survive. I've already found it through ‘Hermes' System’.」
[Activating exclusive skill ‘Lie Detection Lv.7’!]
[You have confirmed that the statement is false.]
“Yoo Sang······.”
「Dokja-ssi.」
She wasn't simply calling my name.
A tone so firm it hardly seemed like Yoo Sangah's.
I remembered a time when we'd worked together as a team.
She'd been like this then, too.
Especially when she was arguing for something she believed was right, Yoo Sangah never backed down. Calmly but firmly, she continued, speaking gently as though soothing a panicking child.
「Dokja-ssi, pull yourself together and listen. Stay calm. Think rationally.」
Why did those words sound familiar?
「I still have a little time. But if you don't save Sookyung-ssi now, it'll be too late.」
Why did my seat feel like a seat on a subway from long ago? Why did this trembling hand feel as though it wasn't mine?
「It's like a game quest. There's a route laid out in advance, and you have to follow it to clear the quest properly.」
“······Yoo Sangah-ssi.”
「And right now, Dokja-ssi, you need to complete the right prerequisite quest.」
I understood what she meant.
Probably better than anyone else in the world.
But I couldn't understand how Yoo Sangah felt as she said it.
Perhaps I never would, even if I spent my whole life trying.
Someone like me shouldn't dare claim to understand.
[‘Fourth Wall’ grows thicker.]
Just as Yoo Sangah had sprung up from her subway seat, I got up and spoke.
“Aileen.”
Understanding my intention, Aileen nodded. The physicians beside Yoo Sangah rushed to the room opposite. I, too, slowly turned and headed toward the other room.
As I crossed the threshold, I couldn't help looking back.
「Don't worry. I'll be waiting here.」
Yoo Sangah's silhouette beyond the curtain had already scattered considerably.
Perhaps the person beyond it was no longer the ‘Yoo Sangah’ I knew.
Perhaps she had been torn apart and scattered into something unrecognizable. Perhaps I was hallucinating the voice of Yoo Sangah, who was already disappearing. Even so,
“Yoo Sangah-ssi. I don't know if you remember······but in the first scenario, I selected whose lives to save.”
I continued speaking to the Yoo Sangah I remembered.
“I allowed only the people I thought I should save to survive. At the time, I thought that was what I had to do. ······I believed that was how I could see this world's ending.”
「······Dokja-ssi.」
“But if doing that again is the only way to see the ‘story's ending’, I'd rather choose not to see it.”
Having to kill someone to save someone else.
“If there are choices like that to make about people's lives, then the story was wrong to begin with.”
Perhaps ‘Mass Production Maker’ would say this about my answer:
That it was ‘a road with no road’.
[‘Fourth Wall’ looks at you.]
But this wasn't a choice.
There had only ever been one road for me.
[Demon King ‘Demon King of Salvation’ looks at ‘Fourth Wall’.]
I wasn't Yoo Joonghyuk.
Even so, on this question, our answers were the same.
“I'll break that ‘story’. So you won't die, Yoo Sangah-ssi. Neither will my mother.”
A wall shrouded in pitch darkness stood before me, blocking the way.
A thick, solid wall that seemed impossible to break through.
Slowly, I reached toward it.
Yoo Joonghyuk and the others returned to Earth an hour later. Yoo Joonghyuk, Han Sooyoung, Lee Jihye, Jung Heewon, Lee Hyunsung, Shin Yoosung, Lee Gilyoung, and Lee Seolhwa.
After safely descending through the portal to the lower scenarios, the first thing they saw was a flash of sparks at the center of the [Industrial Complex].
Tzzzzzzzt!
Sparks of probability crashing down into the heart of the [Factory] like lightning.
Lee Jihye asked:
“······What the hell is going on?”
But no one could give her a proper answer.
The Chimera Dragon beat its wings. Before long, they reached the [Factory]. Jumping down onto the battlements, they ran straight for the hospital rooms.
Seeing them barge in, Flying Fox waved.
“Oh, you're back already?”
Jung Heewon asked:
“Where's Dokja-ssi······No, where's Yoo Sangah-ssi?”
“She's over there―But I think all of you need treatment, too······.”
“We're fine. Just take care of Hyunsung-ssi first.”
“W-wait! I'm fine, too. My skin's just a little scorched―”
“Shut up and lie down.”
After dumping the blackened Lee Hyunsung onto a gurney, Jung Heewon and the others went to Yoo Sangah's room.
They were certain Kim Dokja would have gone there first.
“Dokja-ssi! Sangah-ssi!”
“E-everyone! If you just barge in like that······!”
But what they found was completely unexpected.
Han Sooyoung muttered:
“······What the hell is this?”
Apart from a bare minimum of physicians, there was no sign of anyone in Yoo Sangah's room. Yoo Sangah's soul, still breaking apart. Kim Dokja was nowhere to be seen.
Rrrrrrumble.
A pitch-black Status flowed from Han Sooyoung.
“I asked you a question. What is going on?”
Overwhelmed, the physicians spilled everything, even things she hadn't asked. From the ‘Returnee War’ to what had happened after Kim Dokja arrived.
“······So we began treating Lee Sookyung-ssi first. By now, they should be nearly at the final stage―”
Before the physician could finish, Han Sooyoung moved. Too quickly for anyone to stop her.

Perhaps she'd been living a ‘scenario’ even before the ‘scenarios’ began. No one called it a scenario, but to her, it was a scenario.
If a dokkaebi had named that scenario, perhaps it would have been something like <Declaration of Independence>.
「“I'm Yoo Sangah, a new employee.”」
Joining the game company and moving out of her family home had changed her life a little.
She'd met an interesting person, too.
「“Yoo Sangah-ssi, do you happen to have a phone charger?”」
A pale-faced person who borrowed her charger.
「“I have an important appointment at seven, but my battery's nearly dead.”」
The man who'd attended the new-employee interview with her, who refused to cooperate with anything at the company.
「“I'll come to the company dinner, but I have to head home at seven.”」
Someone who spoke his mind, yet was the first to leave when work ended.
「“I'm not joining the outing. I hate hiking more than anything.”」
A man who wandered like a ghost, looking only at his smartphone as though other people's gazes didn't exist.
「“······That bastard Yoo Joonghyuk's going to die again.”」
Perhaps that was why she, too, had tried doing a few strange things.
Getting back at a superior who stole a subordinate's project. Mixing pepper into the coffee grounds of department heads who sent her on coffee errands.
「“Blech! What is this! What's wrong with this coffee!”」
That was how the historic event at Mino Soft later called the ‘Pantry Incident’ was born.
Pouring pepper again and again into the finely ground coffee, Yoo Sangah felt an inexplicable freedom.
The company in an uproar. A culprit who couldn't be caught, even with an employee keeping watch.
「Yoo Sangah still remembers.」
The office after everyone had gone home.
The faint glow of a smartphone seeping from between the pantry cabinets.
「Kim Dokja had definitely been there.」
Whether she added pepper or salt, that light had simply remained there, silently condoning her actions.
As though anything outside that cabinet were none of his concern.
「Perhaps she should have spoken to him then.」
Why you had stayed silent for me inside that cabinet.
Why you had said, ‘There was no one there,’ even after seeing what I was doing.
Why you had turned the CCTV camera away from the pantry for me.
Why you······only ever showed such a range of expressions when you looked at your smartphone.
Tzzzzzzzt!
Her surroundings brightened, and her senses gradually began to return.
[A powerful being's ‘Status’ does not permit your ‘Stories’ to scatter.]
[Someone who likes things orderly is displeased with your Stories.]
Voices were coming from somewhere.
「(See? This is definitely ‘flirting’.)」
「(No. Having watched nearly every film on Earth, I believe······.)」
「(In the end, isn't it all a desire to become one?)」
When she slowly opened her eyes, she found three beings around her.
A squid-like creature wearing glasses.
An old man with grayish-white hair and a hunched back.
And a beautiful person (美人) with an unusual air, whose gender she couldn't tell.
At the sight of the last being, Yoo Sangah jolted fully awake.
「(You're awake, new librarian.)」
The androgynous beauty, Nirvana, smiled.
Yoo Sangah couldn't make sense of it.
Why was this person here?
With a thoughtful hum, Nirvana studied her and spoke.
「(It's a long story. You'll find out soon. You're very lucky. You're the first being to enter this ‘Library’ after living so few years.)」
Behind the three beings, combinations of letters rippled in the air.
[Welcome, new librarian Yoo Sangah.]
She looked around.
Dim lamplight illuminated patches of darkness.
A library······.
An immense number of books, and shelves with no end in sight. It had been a very long time since she'd entered a library this large.
She remembered Kim Dokja's question. If she lived again, would she be willing to read books other than those by the writers she liked?
······Had this been what he meant?
She didn't know what this place was.
She didn't know how Kim Dokja had sent her here or what he wanted from her.
But she had a feeling.
A feeling that if she read those books now, she could answer the many questions she'd had all this time.
「(Will you read them?)」
「(Pardon?)」
「(You might regret it if you do. The truth might be more than you can bear.)」
Her fingertips paused as she reached toward a book's cover. Not because of Nirvana's words. Someone she knew very well had emerged from the darkness.
“She won't become a librarian.”
Kim Dokja was there.
「(······Dokja-ssi?)」
The moment I saw Yoo Sangah staring blankly at me, profound relief washed over me.
It had worked.
Somehow, I'd succeeded in preserving her soul.
Parts of her soul body were still damaged, but the faintly flowing power of the Library was restoring them.
I bowed my head slightly to her.

“I'm sure there is.”
Tzzzzzzzt!

Nirvana would know.

The first reincarnator.
